extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and practitioners in NLP/LLM evaluation and creative-writing evaluation
extracted.subtask_description: Human evaluation of creative-writing outputs from LLMs (and humans) using a tailored prompt designed to minimize training-data leakage; assessments use a detailed rubric covering aspects such as fluency, style, originality, and humor. The study compares state-of-the-art instruction-tuned commercial and open-source LLMs against human writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluency
rubrics_metrics.description: Fluency (one of the evaluated dimensions listed in the paper's detailed rubric).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation performed by humans using a detailed rubric; the same specifically-tailored prompt was presented to LLMs and human writers. Fluency is assessed as part of comparing model outputs to human outputs on an English creative writing task prompted to force creativity rather than reuse of training data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style
rubrics_metrics.description: Style (one of the evaluated dimensions listed in the paper's detailed rubric).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated by human raters using the study's rubric. The task uses a tailored, unusual prompt (an epic combat between Ignatius J. Reilly and a pterodactyl) to elicit distinct stylistic choices; comparisons are drawn between model and human stylistic output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality (one of the evaluated dimensions listed in the paper's detailed rubric).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humans keep a close lead in originality according to the reported results. The experimental design intentionally minimizes training-data leakage (via a specifically-tailored prompt) to force the models to be creative rather than reuse existing stories; originality is therefore judged under those constraints by human evaluators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor (one of the evaluated dimensions listed in the paper's detailed rubric).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor was assessed by human raters; results indicate only the top three LLMs can handle humor at human-like levels. The same tailored prompt is used across humans and models to evaluate humor elicitation fairly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt design / minimization of training-data leakage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a specifically-tailored prompt to minimize the risk of training-data leakage and force the models to be creative rather than reusing existing stories (methodological desideratum mentioned in the paper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study presents the same unusual prompt (based on an epic combat between Ignatius J. Reilly and a pterodactyl) to both LLMs and human writers so that evaluation focuses on creative ability rather than memorization. This procedural requirement is part of the evaluation standard: prompts should be chosen to reduce overlap with model training data when assessing creativity.
